text:
```yaml
name: Claude Issue Triage

on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]

jobs:
  claude-triage:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write
      id-token: write

    steps:
    - name: Checkout repository
      uses: actions/checkout@v4
      with:
        fetch-depth: 1

    - name: Run Claude Issue Triage
      id: claude-triage
      uses: anthropics/claude-code-action@beta
      with:
        anthropic_api_key: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
        
        # Use GitHub MCP server for issue operations
        mcp_config: |
          {
            "server": "github://github.com/actions/github-mcp-server",
            "capabilities": ["issues"]
          }
        
        # Prompt for issue triage
        prompt: "You are an AI assistant helping with issue triage for the Claude Code SDK Python repository. When a new issue is opened, analyze it and apply appropriate labels based on: - Issue type (bug, feature request, documentation, question, etc.) - Severity level (low, medium, high, critical) - Component affected (client, transport, errors, types, etc.) - Priority (low, medium, high) Apply labels that help categorize and prioritize the issue effectively. For bug reports: - Include severity labels (critical, high, medium, low) - Include component labels (client, transport, errors, types, etc.) - Include status labels (needs-triage, confirmed, reproduction-needed) For feature requests: - Include priority labels (low, medium, high) - Include component labels (client, transport, etc.) - Include status labels (needs-triage, proposal, accepted) For documentation issues: - Include priority labels (low, medium, high) - Include status labels (needs-triage, needs-review) For questions: - Include priority labels (low, medium, high) - Include status labels (needs-triage, answered) Only apply labels that are relevant to the issue content."
```
